Commenter recounts that CoreWeave initially loaded up on GPUs to mine Ethereum, made money during that boom, then pivoted to being a GPU cloud and found itself holding all those GPUs during the ML/AI surge. They called it an "amazing run."
Asked whether crypto-mining GPU operations can convert to AI model services, a user answered: "Yes. Coreweave was an Ethereum mining operation that reconverted into this."
Another user disputed the idea that mining hardware was reused: "No mining GPUs are in their fleet anymore, that's long gone. It's all datacenter GPUs as per their website."

Reacting to the S-1 figure that Microsoft accounted for 35% (2023) and 62% (2024) of CoreWeave revenue, a commenter said: "Wow, I didn't know they where basically a MSFT subsidiary. Who are their other customers?"

One user argued Nvidia's role isn't circular financing. Nvidia's $2b for a 9% stake is only about 5.7% of CoreWeave's $35b 2026 CapEx. In their view, neoclouds take Nvidia investment to secure new chips first and deploy Nvidia's full stack.

Job candidate's experience: CoreWeave "feels very YC-ish." The interviewer asked "very textbook style questions" that the candidate felt you'd only learn in formal schooling for that role. They were rejected despite a referral, after interviewing three times for two different roles.

Reacting to reported Q3 figures of $51.9M operating income against $310M interest expense, a commenter wrote "Holy cow." They also questioned CoreWeave's use of SPVs, which aren't subject to the same regulations as the parent company.

On CoreWeave's bonds turning distressed, commenters said the outcome was "inevitable considering how they financed the build out." One described it as a data center company that "borrowed a lot of money" that the market now doubts it can repay.
